answer: **Hypothesis (data-grounded answer):** The gardening pathway shows different prevalence styles across habitat types in two contrasting contexts. (1) In natural/semi-natural or coastal-wetland habitats, gardening aliens are *proportionally dominant but occur on few plots*: in forests, gardening species make up essentially the entire alien flora (Broad-leaved forests 100%, Coniferous forests ~88% of the few aliens recorded; low-evidence), and in Wetlands and Coastal habitats gardening is the leading pathway, contributing ~55% of alien records and present in ~45–50% of plots — significantly more gardening-dominated than other high-evidence habitats (Wetlands p=6.3e-04, Coastal p=6.7e-03). (2) In the most human-modified, alien-rich habitats — Urban and especially Croplands — gardening's *share* is a minority (29% and 19%, respectively) even though gardening aliens are frequently present (~48% of urban plots), because Unintentional introductions (contaminated seed, trade, tourism) dominate those pools (~69–77% of records); Croplands are significantly gardening-poor relative to other habitats (p=2.2e-04). Riparian and Meadows follow the unintentional-dominated style without significant deviation, and Rock outcrops hold almost no aliens at all (1 record, not gardening). Overall habitat × pathway composition differs highly significantly (pooled chi-square χ²=66.20, df=12, p=1.6e-09; permutation test with fixed margins p=5e-05). As regional temporal context, gardening has become the dominant introduction pathway over time (share of first records rising from 17% before 1500 to 75% in 1985–2019), so the habitat pattern is best read as: gardening prevails as the *introducer* of aliens in natural/coastal-wetland contexts, whereas unintentional introductions prevail in urban and agricultural contexts. Species-level data (gardening = 42/81 species, 52%, the most common pathway overall) is consistent with but does not attribute species to habitats.

payload.hypothesis: The gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants shows different prevalence styles across habitat types: it is proportionally dominant in natural/semi-natural and coastal-wetland habitats — in forests gardening species constitute nearly the entire alien flora (100% in broad-leaved, 88% in coniferous; low-evidence) and in wetlands and coastal habitats it is the leading pathway (~55% of alien records, present in ~45-50% of plots; both significantly more gardening-dominated than other high-evidence habitats, p=6.3e-04 and 6.7e-03) — whereas in the most human-modified, alien-rich habitats (urban, croplands) gardening is a minority share (29% and 19%) despite being frequently present (~48% of urban plots), because unintentional introductions dominate there (69-77% of records; croplands significantly gardening-poor, p=2.2e-04). Habitat x pathway composition differs highly significantly (pooled chi-square 66.20, df=12, p=1.6e-09; permutation p=5e-05). This pattern aligns with the regional temporal trend in which gardening became the dominant introduction pathway over time (share of first records 17% before 1500 to 75% in 1985-2019), suggesting gardening prevails as the introducer of aliens in natural/coastal-wetland contexts while unintentional introductions prevail in urban and agricultural contexts.
payload.workflow: Loaded invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plots, 37 cols, tab-delimited); verified n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo==n.total in all rows (integer counts). Built habitat x pathway contingency table (10 habitats x 3 pathways). Computed per-habitat prevalence styles: gardening share of alien records, per-plot mean gardening count (all plots as denominator incl. n.total=0), per-plot gardening presence frequency, and dominant pathway. Tested composition differences with chi-square after pooling habitats with <10 alien records (Coniferous, Broad-leaved, Scrublands, Rock outcrops), cross-checked with a 20,000-permutation exact test on fixed margins; pairwise 2xK chi-squares for high-evidence habitats. Used invasion_success_pathways.csv (81 species; Gardening 42, Unintentional 30, AgriForest 9) and temporal_trends_contingency_table.csv (regional first records) as context only, not merged; phylogenetic_tree.txt linkage confirmed (76/81 tips) but not required for this question. Caveats documented: counting semantics (species vs occurrences, possible multi-pathway assignment) undocumented; zero-alien plots assumed true absences; small-cell habitats marked low-evidence and excluded from the primary claim.
